docs.syntax: =SUMPRODUCT(heads,salaries) totals a payroll; divide by SUM(heads) for the cost per head
docs.explain: A payroll summary is two columns that only mean something together. Headcount on its own says how many people a team has; salary on its own says what one seat costs. Multiply them row by row and you have the payroll that team represents, and that row-by-row multiplication is exactly what SUMPRODUCT does in one call. The alternative, a helper column of headcount times salary and a SUM underneath, is what most sheets do. It works until someone sorts half the helper column, and doing it in one formula removes that failure. The second half of the lesson is the cost per head, which is the payroll divided by the total headcount rather than the average of the salary column. That distinction is the whole point. Averaging salaries treats a team of one and a team of three as equally important, while dividing by the headcount weighs them the way the money does. Two screens, the payroll and then the cost per head, put the two figures side by side on one table.

screens.prompt: In D2, total the payroll the whole sheet implies.

hints.syntax: =SUMPRODUCT(B2:B5,C2:C5): the headcount column, then the salary column.
hints.func-sumproduct: Each row is headcount times salary, and the rows are then added.
hints.error: Two ranges of different shapes cannot be paired row by row.

the two totals are multiplied, which is not a payroll
the last team is left out of the payroll

the payroll is then divided by zero

the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D2, round the payroll cost of one head to a whole number.

hints.syntax: =ROUND(SUMPRODUCT(B2:B5,C2:C5)/SUM(B2:B5),0): the payroll over the headcount, rounded.
hints.func-sumproduct: The numerator is headcount times salary, added across rows.
hints.func-sum: The denominator is the total headcount, which is a plain sum of the column.
hints.error: A zero headcount total leaves nothing to divide by.

seo.title: Payroll total and cost per head in Excel
seo.description: SUMPRODUCT multiplies headcount by salary row by row in one call, and dividing that payroll by the headcount weighs teams the way the money does.
